title: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Conjunctiva
tocPath: APPROACH TO PATIENTS WITH EMERGENCY CONDITIONS

blocks.text: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of conjunctiva is the major and most common ocular malignancy of the eye in adults. The tumor typically occurs on the bulbar conjunctiva, originating at the limbus, and often spreads onto the cornea, globe, orbit and nasolacrimal system. The cancer is a slow growing tumor of middle-aged to elderly people. It is common in immunocompromised individuals

blocks.text: Table 14.7: Referral Criteria for Eye Conditions
Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes
Pain or redness in one eye, especially with visual and pupillary abnormalities
Recent proptosis of one or both eyes or enlargement of the eye (buphthalmos) in children
Double vision following recent injury (may indicate orbital fracture)
Leukocoria (white pupillary reflex), especially in children
Squint at any age if not previously evaluated by an ophthalmologist
Visual loss in patients with systemic diseases such as diabetes
Refractive errors in teenagers and adults
Long-standing blindness (first presentation to a health facility)
